introduction: Supporting Jain dharma — temples, monks, education, seva, and community — is itself a spiritual practice. Dana (charity) is one of the four essential practices that sustains the Jain Sangha across centuries. Every act of giving purifies the giver's karmic account and strengthens the community for future generations.

templeDonations.title: Temple Construction & Maintenance
templeDonations.description: Temples are the spiritual heart of the Jain community. They are not merely buildings but sacred spaces where Tirthankara idol worship, meditation, and community gathering happen. Supporting temples is supporting the very infrastructure of dharma.
waysToSupport: Financial donations for temple construction and renovation
Volunteer labor for temple maintenance and cleaning
Donation of construction materials (marble, stone, wood)
Sponsoring specific parts of the temple (spires, idols, gates)
Contributing to temple trust funds for long-term sustainability
Providing free accommodation for visiting monks and nuns
templeDonations.significance: Building or maintaining a temple creates massive punya (merit) for the donor and creates a spiritual center that serves thousands for generations. Ancient Jain temples across India have stood for 1,000+ years thanks to such donations.

monkSupport.title: Supporting Monks and Nuns (Sadhu-Sadhvi Seva)
monkSupport.description: Monks and nuns have renounced all possessions and depend entirely on the lay community for basic needs. Supporting them is one of the highest forms of seva because it enables them to dedicate every moment to spiritual practice and teaching.
waysToSupport: Daily alms (Gochari) — preparing pure vegetarian food for monks
Providing clothing (for Svetambara monks), bowls, and whisk brushes
Offering shelter during Chaturmas
Funding travel for Pravachanas and community visits
Paying for medical care when monks require it
Supporting Upadhyayas and Acharyas with study materials and safe passage
monkSupport.significance: Serving a monk or nun is considered equivalent to serving the Tirthankara themselves, as the monk represents the living dharma. Every act of seva toward the Sangha ripples through infinite future lives.

education.title: Jain Education & Pathshala
education.description: Educating children in Jain values, philosophy, and practice is the most long-term investment in the future of the religion. Pathshalas, Sunday schools, and Jain universities preserve and transmit dharma across generations.
waysToSupport: Sponsoring a child's Pathshala education
Donating textbooks, workbooks, and learning materials
Volunteering as a Pathshala teacher or assistant
Funding Jain studies scholarships for university students
Donating to Jain universities (Jain Vishva Bharati, Mumbai University Jain Studies Dept)
Creating online educational content for global Jain diaspora
education.significance: The child who learns Jain values today becomes the elder who preserves dharma tomorrow. Education is the most powerful long-term seva.

scripturePreservation.title: Scripture Preservation & Publication
scripturePreservation.description: Ancient Jain texts are written on palm leaves, paper, and now digital formats. Preserving them requires specialized care. Publishing affordable editions ensures that all Jains, regardless of income, can access canonical texts.
waysToSupport: Donating to manuscript preservation projects
Sponsoring publication of critical editions of Agamas
Supporting translation projects (Prakrit to Hindi to English to Gujarati)
Funding digital libraries and online access
Creating audio versions of scriptures for the visually impaired or busy laypeople
Building temple and community libraries
scripturePreservation.significance: Scriptures are the voice of the Jinas. Losing them means losing the path itself. Every act of preservation protects the dharma for all future souls.

communityService.title: Community Seva & Social Welfare
communityService.description: Jainism extends Ahimsa beyond the Jain community to all beings. Community service is a practical expression of Aparigraha — giving rather than accumulating — and of compassion for all suffering beings.
waysToSupport: Food drives and hunger relief programs
Medical camps and free health clinics in underserved areas
Animal shelters and cow protection (Goshala) support
Educational scholarships for poor students regardless of religion
Disaster relief and emergency humanitarian aid
Environmental projects: tree planting, river cleanup, plastic reduction
Elder care and orphanage support
communityService.significance: Jainism is not merely personal liberation but collective upliftment. The community that serves others creates the conditions for universal peace. Social welfare is the practical application of Ahimsa at scale.

diasporaSupport.title: Supporting the Global Jain Diaspora
diasporaSupport.description: Millions of Jains now live outside India. Maintaining Jain practice abroad requires temples, Pathshalas, community centers, and spiritual teachers. Supporting diaspora communities spreads dharma globally.
waysToSupport: Donate to build Jain temples in new diaspora locations
Fund traveling monks who visit diaspora communities for Chaturmas
Create online resources for children growing up outside India
Support Jain student associations at universities worldwide
Donate to interfaith initiatives that introduce Jain values to broader society
Volunteer to teach or mentor Jain youth in foreign cities
diasporaSupport.significance: Jainism is a global path, not an Indian one. Supporting diaspora communities ensures that Jain wisdom is available to all seekers everywhere, fulfilling the universal vision of Ahimsa.
